Electric Shock Hazards: Damp work gloves drastically decrease electrical resistance between the welder and live electrode holders.
Metal Fume Control: Inhaling vaporized zinc oxides from galvanized steel causes severe systemic metal fume fever.

misconception_pool.fact: Plasma cutters use an electric arc to superheat non-flammable gases like compressed air or nitrogen into an ionized plasma jet.

misconception_pool.misconception: Mechanical shearing and bandsaw cutting leave a wide heat-affected zone that hardens the cut edge of mild steel plate.
misconception_pool.fact: Mechanical cutting severs metal through cold shear or chip removal, avoiding the thermal distortion and hardening of torch cuts.

misconception_pool.misconception: Using a graphite pencil or permanent ink marker instead of soapstone is ideal for sketching layout lines on hot steel.

misconception_pool.misconception: Holding a very long arc length helps the molten filler metal spread out wider and penetrate deeper into a fillet joint.
misconception_pool.fact: An overly long arc scatters heat, increases spatter, reduces root penetration, and lets atmospheric gases cause weld porosity.

misconception_pool.misconception: Welding is strictly manual shop labor with zero opportunities for advanced technical education.
misconception_pool.fact: Welding engineering degrees combine metallurgy, automated robotics, computer-aided design, and destructive testing science.

misconception_pool.misconception: Passing a single welding certification test qualifies a welder to perform every welding process on any metal thickness.
misconception_pool.fact: Welder performance qualifications apply only to the specific process, position, base metal group, and thickness range tested.

misconception_pool.misconception: An AWS Welding Certification lasts for life without requiring ongoing continuity logs or periodic employer verification.
misconception_pool.fact: AWS welder certification requires signed continuity verification every six months confirming the welder still uses that process.

misconception_pool.misconception: Careers in the welding industry are limited to manual shop floor production work with no pathways into engineering.
misconception_pool.fact: Welding careers span robotics programming, metallurgical engineering, nondestructive testing, and certified code inspection.

misconception_pool.misconception: The American Welding Society is a federal government agency that issues criminal fines to local metal fabrication shops.
misconception_pool.fact: The American Welding Society is a nonprofit professional organization that publishes consensus standards and administers exams.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why must a welder wear a properly shaded welding helmet (such as Shade 10 to 13 for arc welding) and flame-resistant leather or heavy cotton clothing rather than synthetic polyester or fleece?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why must a welder wear a properly shaded welding helmet (such as Shade 10 to 13 for arc welding) and flame-resistant leather or heavy cotton clothing rather than synthetic polyester or fleece?
options: A. The welding arc emits intense ultraviolet and infrared radiation that causes painful corneal flash burns ('arc eye') and skin burns.
B. A clear plastic face shield blocks all ultraviolet arc rays, and polyester fleece reflects molten spatter better than leather.
C. Welding helmets are only needed to keep smoke out of your eyes, and synthetic gym shorts keep the welder cool during overhead passes.
D. Sunglasses provide enough shade protection for MIG and stick welding as long as you squint during the strike.
choices: A. The welding arc emits intense ultraviolet and infrared radiation that causes painful corneal flash burns ('arc eye') and skin burns.
B. A clear plastic face shield blocks all ultraviolet arc rays, and polyester fleece reflects molten spatter better than leather.
C. Welding helmets are only needed to keep smoke out of your eyes, and synthetic gym shorts keep the welder cool during overhead passes.
D. Sunglasses provide enough shade protection for MIG and stick welding as long as you squint during the strike.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. The welding arc emits intense ultraviolet and infrared radiation that causes painful corneal flash burns ('arc eye') and skin burns, while sparks and hot slag can melt synthetic fabrics directly into the skin.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): An electric welding arc produces intense UV and IR radiation that burns unprotected retinas and corneas in seconds, and hot slag ignites or melts synthetic fabrics like nylon or polyester onto skin.

patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which section of a Safety Data Sheet (SDS) specifies the exposure limits and personal protective equipment required when working with welding consumables?
options: A. Exposure Controls and Personal Protection
B. Physical and Chemical Properties

D. Transport and Regulatory Information
choices: A. Exposure Controls and Personal Protection
B. Physical and Chemical Properties

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Exposure Controls and Personal Protection
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): The Exposure Controls/Personal Protection section of an SDS identifies airborne exposure limits and specifies the protective gear needed to minimize worker exposure (p. 13).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Approximately how hot does the electric arc get to melt both the electrode tip and the base metal during arc welding?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Approximately how hot does the electric arc get to melt both the electrode tip and the base metal during arc welding?
options: A. Around 1,200 degrees Fahrenheit
B. Roughly 3,500 degrees Fahrenheit
C. Just under 5,000 degrees Fahrenheit
D. Above 9,000 degrees Fahrenheit
choices: A. Around 1,200 degrees Fahrenheit
B. Roughly 3,500 degrees Fahrenheit
C. Just under 5,000 degrees Fahrenheit
D. Above 9,000 degrees Fahrenheit
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): The electric arc generates intense heat measuring above 9,000 degrees Fahrenheit, which rapidly melts both the tip of the electrode and the base metal surface (p. 32).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why is shielded metal arc equipment particularly well-suited for outdoor construction and remote repair work?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why is shielded metal arc equipment particularly well-suited for outdoor construction and remote repair work?
options: A. It produces zero fumes and never requires ventilation
B. It is portable with engine generators and resists wind drafts
C. It uses an endless spool of wire that never needs changing
D. It operates without any electrical current or ground clamp
choices: A. It produces zero fumes and never requires ventilation
B. It is portable with engine generators and resists wind drafts
C. It uses an endless spool of wire that never needs changing
D. It operates without any electrical current or ground clamp
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. It is portable with engine generators and resists wind drafts
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Shielded metal arc equipment can be powered by portable gasoline or diesel generators and is much less sensitive to outdoor wind and drafts than gas-shielded processes (p. 39).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why must you inspect oxygen regulators, hoses, and torch fittings to ensure they are completely free of oil and grease before connecting them?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why must you inspect oxygen regulators, hoses, and torch fittings to ensure they are completely free of oil and grease before connecting them?
options: A. Grease clogs the ground clamp and reduces electrical conductivity
B. Oil makes the torch handle slippery and harder to aim
C. Pure oxygen can react violently with oil or grease and explode
D. Lubricant turns the welding arc flame from blue to yellow
choices: A. Grease clogs the ground clamp and reduces electrical conductivity
B. Oil makes the torch handle slippery and harder to aim
C. Pure oxygen can react violently with oil or grease and explode
D. Lubricant turns the welding arc flame from blue to yellow
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Pure oxygen can react violently with oil or grease and explode
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Pressurized oxygen reacts violently with hydrocarbons, so all regulators, hoses, and fittings must be tight and completely free of oil or grease to prevent fires or explosions (p. 21).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: During oxy-fuel equipment shutdown, what should you do after closing the main cylinder valves and draining the gas from each hose?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: During oxy-fuel equipment shutdown, what should you do after closing the main cylinder valves and draining the gas from each hose?
options: A. Release the adjusting screws on both gas regulators
B. Disconnect the regulators from the cylinders immediately
C. Open both torch valves simultaneously and leave them open
D. Submerge the hot torch tip in a bucket of cold water
choices: A. Release the adjusting screws on both gas regulators
B. Disconnect the regulators from the cylinders immediately
C. Open both torch valves simultaneously and leave them open
D. Submerge the hot torch tip in a bucket of cold water
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Release the adjusting screws on both gas regulators
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): After closing the cylinder valves and bleeding each line individually, you must release the adjusting screws on both the oxygen and fuel-gas regulators to relieve spring tension (p. 71).
